signal.levels: first depth_levels validated levels on each side of the sealed or replayed book
signal.formula: B = sum(bid px x bid sz), A = sum(ask px x ask sz), total = B + A, I = (B - A) / total, spread_bps = 10000 x (best ask - best bid) / ((best ask + best bid) / 2). All comparisons use exact rational arithmetic; floats are for display only.
signal.qualifying: an observation qualifies long when I > entry_threshold and short when I < -entry_threshold (strict), with spread_bps <= max_spread_bps, total >= min_combined_depth_usd and total > 0. Equality to the threshold is neutral. A side with fewer than depth_levels levels does not qualify (insufficient_depth).
signal.eligibility: each confirming observation has event and first receipt at or before D, satisfies the contract time bounds and has a distinct source identity; the newest (crossing) observation has D - event <= max_snapshot_age_ms and D - receipt <= max_snapshot_age_ms
signal.episode: a maximal same-direction run of distinct qualifying observations after a proven boundary. A neutral observation, a spread or depth filter failure, the other direction, or any reset marker (epoch_start, subscribed, subscription_failed, disconnected, invalid_frame, conflict, out_of_order, clock_regression, silence, evidence_loss, depth_raised) ends it. A boundary is proven by a retained marker or a retained non-qualifying observation; if the window holds neither before the run, the result is evidence_truncated and entries hold.
signal.crossing: the Nth qualifying observation, N = confirmation_observations; crossing time = max(event, first receipt) of that observation
signal.deadline: the sole decision deadline is the smallest UTC whole second at or above the crossing time. The entry is emitted only if the episode is still the active valid run at D and its evidence is eligible. A break before D cancels the opportunity.
signal.consumption: the episode is consumed at its deadline whether a position is open, a risk limit blocks, a fill fails or the deadline is skipped. Later intervals return a consumed hold. A missed deadline never catches up.
signal.identity: episode identity = sha256 over contract, source key, specification hash, effective parameter JSON, boundary identity, direction and first qualifying observation identity; entry identity = sha256 over episode identity, crossing observation identity and deadline. The same interval and input always return the same decision and identity.
signal.diagnostics: every result records deadline, source/contract/specification hashes, episode and entry identity when defined, used observation identities, B, A, total, I, spread_bps, ages, confirmation count, state and reason
signal.failure_outcome: missing, malformed, stale, conflicting or incomplete book evidence gives signal 0 with a stable reason; invalid parameters are refused before any data is read

validation.min_combined_depth_usd: finite positive quote notional, at most 1000000000
validation.rules: booleans are not numbers; fractional integers, unknown keys, non-finite values and unsupported combinations are refused before data acquisition; Go requirement extraction and the Python registry mirror one validator

parameters.search_family: the full Cartesian product (972 variants); every variant is scored on every split and published
parameters.note: research seeds, not endorsed trading settings; the depth contract and the fixed values are never optimized

exit_and_risk.stop_owner: scalar stop_loss_atr_mult 1.0; ATR = simple mean of the true range of the 14 most recent complete derived 1m bars before the entry fill minute, which needs the 15 most recent closed minutes complete; frozen at the entry fill; missing ATR prevents entry (missing_atr)
exit_and_risk.bars_held: integer count of complete one-minute durations since the entry fill
exit_and_risk.no_other_owner: no close fallback, reversal close, trailing stop, scale-in, hedge or take-profit
exit_and_risk.pre_entry_stop_bound: entry refused when the stop distance times size exceeds 1% of current equity (refusal bound only)
exit_and_risk.portfolio_controls: 2% UTC daily realized-loss entry hold; 10% peak-equity drawdown entry latch; pause and unreadable portfolio marks hold new exposure; closes continue
exit_and_risk.protection_order: protection and risk exits apply before elective entries at a deadline
exit_and_risk.liquidation: isolated 1x: a long cannot be liquidated above zero and a short only after about a 100% rise, so the 1 ATR stop is always inside the liquidation bound; the existing clamp is applied and unresolved stop geometry (ATR <= 0) refuses the entry

latency.direct_owner_scenario: labeled separately with zero transport delay; never represents the shared consumer

execution.fill_book: the first accepted archive book with event and receipt strictly after D and both at or after D + 5000 + processing; it must have receipt at most 10000 ms after that executable time, else the entry fails (no_executable_book) and the episode stays consumed
execution.depth_walk: buys walk asks in ascending price, sells walk bids in descending price; requested and available quantity are lot-floored; same-time intents share depth once in stable coin, strategy, identity order; actual weighted prices and fees are booked
execution.partial: one immediate-or-cancel attempt per entry identity; the remainder is cancelled; no resubmission
execution.minimums: entries below the pinned venue minimum notional are refused; a full reduce-only close uses the frozen venue remainder rule; no close exceeds held size; partial closes keep entry ATR and sizing geometry
execution.exits: time stop: at the first whole second at or after fill + 5 x 60000 ms, a close request executes like an entry (5000 + processing ms, first later book, at most 10000 ms after the executable time, else it stays pending and retries on each later book). ATR stop: a mark row at minute t with mark_px <= stop (long) or >= stop (short) triggers a venue-side close at the first accepted book with event and receipt after t (no added latency). A pending close is never booked without a book; minutes held without a mark row are a held-coverage gap.

costs.spread: inside the walked bid/ask; no half spread is added
costs.funding: hourly fundingHistory rates (public info API, fetched once and hash-pinned), charged at each funding time T with the position open at T (entry fill < T <= exit fill): payment = size x oracle_px(T) x rate, a long pays a positive rate; pre-fee realized and net results are kept separate

execution.marks: mark_px rows from asset_ctxs, usable from their row time; funding uses oracle_px of the funding-hour row
execution.unresolvable_order: a window where the event stream cannot resolve liquidation or stop/exit order is reported unsupported and inconclusive
execution.terminal_inventory: marked separately and never labeled a venue close; missing exit prices prevent net scoring
execution.replay_order: resets and timers apply before a same-time decision; books apply before a decision only when event and receipt are both at or before it; tie order is receipt time, source key, local sequence; funding and candles use their own availability times
execution.sizing_detail: target notional = margin 100 x leverage 1; quantity = floor(100 / reference price) to the lot step 10^-szDecimals (BTC 5, ETH 4 from pinned venue meta), reference = best ask for a buy and best bid for a sell of the fill book; the walk fills at most that quantity over up to 20 levels; filled notional under 10 USD is refused

comparator.bars: derived one-minute bars (data_plan.derived_bars), complete bars only
comparator.entries: native mirrored entry columns through the registry; the explicit native close owner suppresses its open-fallback exits
comparator.opportunity: one per coin per complete derived bar whose donchian entry column is nonzero; decision at the bar close m + 60000 ms
comparator.fill: no earlier than the next bar open and the first later latency-eligible executable book
comparator.identical: data eligibility, stops, time close, capital, fees, latency, lot and minimum rules, risk and portfolio limits, and the same event simulator

splits.rule: whole UTC days in order: train = round(0.6 x 59) = 35, validation = round(0.2 x 59) = 12, held-out = the remaining 12

objects.books: market_data/YYYYMMDD/H/l2Book/{BTC,ETH}.lz4 for every hour of the window (2832 keys); 2026-07-17 is the unscored lookback day and its book objects are listed as absent, so the window starts a new session at 2026-07-18T00:00:00Z
objects.asset_ctxs: asset_ctxs/YYYYMMDD.csv.lz4 for every window day plus 2026-07-17
objects.funding: fundingHistory for BTC and ETH from 2026-07-17T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-15T01:00:00Z
objects.venue_meta: meta (szDecimals, maxLeverage, marginTables), pinned once; BTC and ETH size decimals are assumed unchanged over the window

data_plan.storage: raw objects and derived series stay in backtest/candidates/order_book_imbalance_1635/data/archive/ (ignored by git); data/archive_manifest.json in git pins each S3 key, size and sha256 (absent keys listed as absent)
data_plan.import: backtest/book_archive.py with the research need (window 60000, capacity 4096, depth 20) and docs/research/1635-l2-book-archive-note.md; lookback hours start the epoch, so the window's first evidence is not a fresh epoch
data_plan.derived_bars: for each coin and UTC minute [m, m + 60000): the accepted books with receipt in the minute; mid = (best bid px + best ask px) / 2; open = first mid, high = max mid, low = min mid, close = last mid. A bar is complete when at least one book is present, the first receipt is at most 10000 ms after m, the last receipt is at most 10000 ms before m + 60000, and no marker has a time in the minute. A bar is available at m + 60000.
data_plan.lookback: evidence windows, derived bars and ATR may use data before a split start; no entry or score is taken from it
data_plan.purge: no entry decision in the last 5 minutes of a split; after a split end only exits run, and a position still open 30 minutes after the end is terminal inventory (reported, not counted as closed); each split starts flat

eligibility.eligible_day: both coins have all 24 book hour objects, 1440 asset_ctxs rows each and 24 funding rows each, and at least 99% of the day's minutes have complete derived bars for both coins
eligibility.ineligible_day: no entry decision on an ineligible day (both arms); exits continue
eligibility.opportunity: a coin-minute; usable when the derived bar is complete, the asset_ctxs row is present and the book state is covered at the bar close
eligibility.opportunity_coverage: at least 99% of coin-minutes on the eligible days of each scored split are usable; ineligible days, which allow no entry in either arm, are outside the gate and are reported separately
eligibility.held_hour_coverage: every held minute has a mark row, every crossed funding hour has a rate and an oracle_px row, and every close fills from a book; any gap makes the held coverage incomplete
eligibility.integrity: any manifest sha256 or size mismatch, LZ4 checksum failure or importer error stops the run as invalid
eligibility.coverage_clarification: Clarified before any PnL was computed: the original text did not say whether ineligible days count toward the 99% gate. Ineligible days allow no entries in either arm, so they cannot bias the arm comparison; sample size stays bounded by the 30-eligible-day minimum and the 100 held-out positions per arm. No other rule changed, including the 1440-row eligible-day rule.

selection_rule: training selects the greatest train net result among complete variants; ties choose the lexicographically smallest parameter JSON (sorted keys, compact separators); validation freezes the selected variant and reports all variants; held-out values never change the choice

bootstrap.method: UTC-day block bootstrap of the held-out daily paired difference (candidate net minus comparator net, by day of close)
bootstrap.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(1635), integers over the held-out day indexes
bootstrap.statistic: sum of the resampled daily differences

pass_if_all: bootstrap lower bound of the paired improvement > 0
at least two of three held-out blocks with positive improvement
candidate maximum drawdown no worse than the comparator
selected variant net result > 0 at each processing stress (500 and 1000 ms)
net result > 0 for a majority of the selected variant's available one-axis neighbors
verdict.fail: a complete scored run that misses any pass requirement
verdict.inconclusive: insufficient evidence: fewer than 30 eligible days, fewer than three held-out blocks, fewer than 100 closed held-out positions in either arm, coverage below the gates, or missing cost, funding, mark or exit evidence
verdict.published: every attempted variant with net return, maximum drawdown, turnover, fees, funding, coin and direction concentration and independent position totals, including negative results and parameter neighbors
verdict.live_status: production_refused for every outcome; promotion needs a separate reviewed decision
verdict.neighbors: one-axis neighbors: change one parameter to the adjacent value in its search list, others fixed; scored on the held-out split
verdict.complete_variant: a variant is complete on a split when that split meets the opportunity and held-hour coverage gates
